hero.headline: Proposed federal rule would allow cancellation of research grants at any time
hero.body:
The federal government has proposed new funding rules that would permit officials to cancel research grants at any time, according to documents describing the regulatory changes. The proposal would also make peer review optional for grant applications and introduce political staff screening of grants for forbidden topics.

The changes represent a shift in how federal research funding would be administered. Under current practice, research grants typically undergo peer review by scientific experts and include defined terms and conditions. The proposed rules would give administrators broader authority to terminate funding arrangements.

Political appointees would gain the ability to screen grant applications for subject matter deemed off limits. This review process would occur alongside or in place of traditional scientific peer review, which has historically served as the primary evaluation mechanism for research proposals.

The peer review system has traditionally involved scientists and subject matter experts assessing the merit and methodology of proposed research. Making this process optional would alter how grant applications are evaluated before funding decisions are made.

The proposal to allow grant cancellations at any time would affect ongoing research projects. Current grant agreements typically specify terms, timelines, and conditions under which funding can be withdrawn. Removing these constraints would give funding agencies more flexibility to end support for research already underway.

Researchers rely on multi-year grants to conduct studies, hire staff, and maintain laboratory operations. The ability to cancel grants without defined cause or process could affect planning and execution of long-term research projects.

The introduction of political staff into the grant screening process adds a layer of review focused on topic restrictions. This differs from scientific peer review, which evaluates research quality, methodology, and potential contributions to a field of study.

The proposed rules have not yet been finalized. Federal regulatory changes typically undergo a comment period before implementation, allowing affected parties and the public to submit feedback on proposed policies.

cards.headline: Iranian Missile Strike Injures Americans at Kuwaiti Air Base
cards.body:
American personnel were injured when Iran launched a major retaliatory strike against a Kuwaiti air base, escalating tensions in the Middle East. The attack was one of more than 25 waves of strikes that Iran launched in response to a US-Israeli bombing campaign carried out against the country on Saturday.

The Iranian assault targeted military installations across the region, including US bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, and other locations. British personnel stationed near the US naval base in Bahrain came within 200 metres of an Iranian missile and drone strike, though no British casualties were reported. In Iraq, an Iranian missile landed approximately 400 metres from UK personnel involved in counter-Islamic State operations.

Beyond military targets, Iranian attacks also struck civilian infrastructure previously considered relatively safe. Strikes hit Kuwait's airport, the Fairmont hotel in Dubai, and a skyscraper in Bahrain. Iran also fired two missiles into the eastern Mediterranean Sea in the direction of Cyprus, which officials believed may have been aimed at the US Navy's Ford carrier strike group operating in the area.

The scale of the Iranian response reflected the severity of the preceding US-Israeli operation. According to British Defence Secretary John Healey, Iran was "lashing out in an increasingly indiscriminate and widespread way." He expressed concern that the strikes were not limited to military targets, noting that civilian airports, hotels, and other civilian areas had been hit.

British forces actively engaged in regional defence operations to support allies under attack. RAF Typhoon jets shot down an Iranian drone over Iraq heading for a Western base, and another drone bound for Qatar was intercepted by a Typhoon using an air-to-air missile. British jets from RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus and the American Al Udeid airbase in Qatar were mobilised to defend against slower-moving cruise missiles and drones, though officials acknowledged these systems cannot effectively stop faster ballistic missiles.

The UK, while not participating in the US-Israeli attack on Iran, strengthened its defensive posture across the region. All British personnel in the Middle East were reported safe and accounted for, though troops remained on high alert with their positioning under review as the conflict developed.

The Iranian strikes followed the US-Israeli bombing campaign that killed Iran's supreme leader, Ali Khamenei, and other senior officials. Iran's retaliatory attacks targeted multiple countries in the region, including Israel, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Jordan, demonstrating the widespread impact of the escalating conflict.

Healey defended Britain's defensive role, stating that the UK was acting to protect both civilian sites and military assets across the region. The incident marked a significant escalation in the conflict's reach beyond traditional military zones.

cards.headline: Nine workers confirmed dead in Longview paper mill disaster
cards.body:
A chemical tank rupture at a paper mill in Longview, Washington has claimed nine lives, with two workers still unaccounted for. The disaster occurred Tuesday morning at the Nippon Dynawave Packaging Co facility when an industrial tank holding white liquor ruptured and released its contents across the site.

Recovery crews have retrieved the remains of seven victims so far. The operation shifted from rescue to recovery efforts after authorities determined there was no possibility of finding additional survivors. Matt Amos with the Longview fire department said the recovery process would be "slow, methodical and deliberate," with recovered victims undergoing decontamination before transport to the coroner.

White liquor is a caustic chemical mixture made primarily of sodium hydroxide and sodium sulfide, used in the paper industry to break down wood for kraft paper production. The ruptured tank held approximately 600,000 gallons of the liquid. An additional 25,000 gallons remains in the damaged tank and is slowly leaking into surrounding areas.

The incident sent white liquor spilling into a drainage ditch and contaminating the Columbia River. Dead carp were found following the spill. Officials urged the public to avoid ditches and dikes while water testing continues, though they reported no threats to air quality or drinking water in the city of 40,000.

Among the victims were two brothers who worked together at the facility, a trivia champion, and an electrician known for helping farmer neighbors. One worker had arrived early to attend an ultrasound appointment with his partner.

Washington Governor Bob Ferguson stated authorities were "bracing ourselves for this being the deadliest industrial tragedy in modern Washington state history." The sprawling Longview plant employs about 1,000 people and manufactures materials for tissues, printing paper, cups, plates and cartons.

The U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board announced it was launching a federal investigation into the tank failure. The cause remains unknown. Safety complaints were filed against Nippon Dynawave in March and May, though authorities said both were unrelated to the current situation. The company has faced three separate health and safety violations since 2021, resulting in a $3,400 fine.

During a news conference, Brian Wood with Nippon Dynawave stated the company was focused on victims and cooperating with first responders. He pledged the company would "cooperate to the maximum extent" with investigators.

At a community vigil, residents gathered to pray and light candles as families waited for answers. Crystal Moldenhauer, a Longview resident with friends at the plant, expressed the community's uncertainty: "There's families that have been torn apart, and we don't know why."

The facility remains closed as investigations continue.

cards.headline: Germany Deploys Troops to Lithuania Amid Russian Threat
cards.teaser: Berlin has stationed forces in the Baltic nation, which was once occupied by Germany during World War II.
cards.body:
Germany has deployed military forces to Lithuania to protect the Baltic nation amid concerns about Russian aggression in Europe. The deployment marks a significant historical shift, given that Germany occupied Lithuania during World War II.

This time, Lithuanian officials and residents have welcomed the German troops as a protective measure against potential Russian military action. The presence represents a change in how Lithuania views German military involvement in the region.

cards.headline: US Defense Secretary Tells Asian Allies to Increase Defense Spending
cards.teaser: Defense Secretary Hegseth addressed questions about American commitment to the region at a security summit in Singapore.
cards.body:
US Defense Secretary Hegseth reassured Asian allies at a security summit in Singapore that America remains committed to the region. However, he emphasized that partner nations must strengthen their own defense capabilities.

Hegseth fielded questions about US security commitments and future arms sales to allied nations as regional powers evaluate the reliability of American security guarantees amid ongoing global tensions.

cards.headline: SpaceX awarded $4.16 billion contract for missile-tracking satellites
cards.teaser: The U.S. Space Force selected SpaceX to build a network of satellites designed to track airborne targets.
cards.body:
The U.S. Space Force awarded SpaceX a $4.16 billion contract to develop satellites for the Golden Dome defense system. The sensor-equipped satellites will detect and track airborne targets from space, strengthening the military's missile defense capabilities.

This contract is part of SpaceX's growing relationship with the Pentagon. The company revealed in recent filings that government contracts already represent a significant portion of its revenue, underscoring the importance of defense work to its business operations.

cards.headline: SEC proposes repeal of climate disclosure rule for companies
cards.teaser: The securities regulator moved to eliminate requirements for corporate reporting of greenhouse gas emissions and climate risk.
cards.body:
The Securities and Exchange Commission proposed repealing a rule that requires companies to disclose greenhouse gas emissions and climate-related risks. The move would eliminate climate disclosure requirements established during the previous administration.

The proposed action would remove mandatory reporting standards for corporate climate data. The rule had required publicly traded companies to report their environmental impact and climate-related financial risks to investors.

cards.headline: Vietnam Leader Warns Against Superpower Conflict in Asia
cards.teaser: To Lam addressed military leaders from across the region about growing tensions and eroding international norms.
cards.body:
Vietnamese leader To Lam warned military leaders from across Asia about the risks of superpower conflict, saying distrust and disrespect for established rules have created a dangerous environment. He described the current situation as one where the big fish swallow the small fish.

To Lam delivered the speech to regional military leaders gathered for discussions on security matters. His remarks addressed concerns about how major powers interact with smaller nations in the region.

cards.headline: Germany Deploys Troops to Lithuania Amid Russian Threat
cards.teaser: Berlin has stationed forces in the Baltic nation, which was once occupied by Germany during World War II.
cards.body:

cards.headline: Ships Turn Off Transponders to Exit Strait of Hormuz
cards.teaser: Vessels are sailing without tracking signals to escape the waterway affected by the Iran conflict.
cards.body:
Ships are turning off their transponders to sneak out of the Strait of Hormuz without detection. About one quarter of large oil tankers that had been trapped by the Iran conflict have escaped the area using this method.

Data shows a greater proportion of non-Iranian vessels are now crossing the strait. Three oil and liquefied natural gas tankers recently exited the waterway with their transponders turned off, while overall traffic through the strait has declined as reopening efforts make limited progress.

cards.headline: Canadian Man Pleads Guilty to Aiding Suicides Worldwide
cards.teaser: Kenneth Law admitted to sending suicide packets to hundreds of people around the world.
cards.body:
Kenneth Law, a Canadian man, pleaded guilty to 14 counts of assisting suicide after mailing "suicide packets" containing lethal chemicals to more than 100 people across dozens of countries, including Canada, the UK, the US, Italy, Australia and New Zealand. He appeared in an Ontario courtroom after prosecutors withdrew 14 murder charges in exchange for his guilty plea.

Law included instructions with the toxic chemicals he sold online. Families of victims have questioned how he was able to operate his business for so long, calling the process too easy. UK authorities say at least 79 deaths in Britain are connected to Law's actions, though families are pushing for additional charges to be filed in the UK. Sentencing is scheduled for September.

cards.headline: Spain's Prime Minister Faces Corruption Probes
cards.teaser: Pedro Sánchez is fighting for political survival as investigations target colleagues and relatives.
cards.body:
Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez is facing multiple corruption investigations after eight years in office. Probes targeting his colleagues and relatives have put him in a fight for political survival.

Sánchez has refused to step down despite the wave of scandals surrounding his administration. The corruption investigations involve people in his inner circle, creating pressure on his continued leadership of the Spanish government.

cards.headline: U.S. strikes boat in Pacific, death toll from operations exceeds 200
cards.teaser: Another U.S. military strike on an alleged drug boat killed three people in the eastern Pacific Ocean.
cards.body:
The U.S. military carried out another strike on Friday against a boat in the eastern Pacific Ocean, killing three men. This was the third such attack this week as part of an ongoing campaign against vessels accused of drug smuggling. The strike pushed the overall death toll from these operations above 200 people.

U.S. Southern Command said the vessel was engaged in narco-trafficking operations and operated by a designated terrorist organization.

cards.headline: Judge orders Kennedy Center to remove Trump name from building
cards.teaser: A federal judge ruled that the Kennedy Center must remove references to Trump from the facility.
cards.body:
A federal judge has ordered the Kennedy Center to remove Trump's name from the building. The ruling also blocked a planned two-year closure for renovations that Trump had announced, requiring the performing arts venue to remain open to the public.

Trump responded to the decision by stating he has no further interest in the Kennedy Center following the court's order to remove his name from the facility.

cards.headline: Bondi tells lawmakers redaction errors occurred in Epstein files release
cards.teaser: Former Attorney General Pam Bondi testified before Congress about the handling of Jeffrey Epstein files.
cards.body:
Pam Bondi, the former US attorney general, testified before a House panel about mistakes made when her Justice Department released files related to Jeffrey Epstein. During the congressional probe, she attributed responsibility for the redaction errors to Todd Blanche and Kash Patel, who served under her at the department.

The testimony occurred roughly a month after Bondi was removed from her position by President Donald Trump. According to congressional observers, her statements placing blame on Blanche are likely to make him a focus of Democratic investigations into the matter.

cards.headline: No Iran deal announced after Trump White House meeting
cards.teaser: President Trump met with advisers but did not announce a final decision on a proposed agreement with Iran.
cards.body:
Trump met with his advisers at the White House to make a final decision on Iran negotiations. U.S. and Iranian officials had previously agreed on a framework for a potential deal, but no agreement was announced following the meeting.

Pentagon Chief Pete Hegseth stated that the U.S. military is prepared to resume military operations against Iran if negotiations fail to reach an agreement.

cards.headline: Trump physician reports president in excellent health
cards.teaser: The White House released results from Trump's latest physical examination.
cards.body:
Trump's physician said the president is in excellent health and fully fit to serve following a physical examination. The doctor recommended Trump lose weight and exercise more but concluded he was in excellent health overall.

The medical report noted Trump had leg swelling and hand bruising. The White House released the results of the physical exam, which found the president capable of carrying out his duties despite the recommendations for lifestyle changes.

cards.headline: Trump endorses opponents of Nancy Mace in South Carolina governor race
cards.teaser: The president backed Pamela Evette for South Carolina governor instead of Representative Nancy Mace.
cards.body:
Trump endorsed Pamela Evette in the Republican primary for South Carolina governor, snubbing Representative Nancy Mace who had been seeking his support. The president also jumped into other state races, endorsing Randy Feenstra for governor in the Iowa primary.

Trump's endorsements span multiple Republican primaries for governor in South Carolina, Iowa, and Oklahoma. The decision to back Evette over Mace represents a break with the incumbent congresswoman from South Carolina's coastal district.

hero.headline: Blue Origin rocket explodes during test at Cape Canaveral
hero.body:
A Blue Origin New Glenn rocket exploded during a static fire test at Launch Complex 36 in Cape Canaveral, Florida on Thursday evening at 9pm ET. The massive fireball engulfed and destroyed the launchpad seconds after the scheduled "hotfire" test began. The explosion was visible across a wide area, with an orange sky reported in Fort Pierce, 115 miles to the south, and shockwaves felt by residents in nearby communities and as far north as South Carolina.

Blue Origin confirmed that all employees were safe and unaccounted for following the incident. The company described the explosion as "an anomaly" on social media. Jeff Bezos, the company's founder, acknowledged it was "a very rough day" but expressed commitment to investigating the cause and returning to flight operations.

The explosion carries significant implications for NASA's lunar program. Just two days before the test failure, NASA had announced that Blue Origin won a contract to launch the first of three planned uncrewed lunar missions this year to begin construction of a $20 billion moon base. The New Glenn rocket is the vehicle Blue Origin intends to use to launch lunar landers for NASA, including those that will carry astronauts to the lunar surface as part of the Artemis program.

NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman stated that the agency would conduct a full evaluation of the timeline for the Artemis program and lunar base construction following the explosion. "Spaceflight is unforgiving, and developing new heavy-lift launch capability is extraordinarily difficult," Isaacman wrote. NASA said it would work with Blue Origin to support a thorough investigation and assess the impact on near-term missions.

This explosion represents the latest in a series of setbacks for Blue Origin as it competes with SpaceX for NASA contracts. The company's third New Glenn flight in the previous month ended with a payload in the wrong orbit, resulting in a temporary FAA grounding. Thursday's static fire test was the first since the FAA cleared the rocket to resume flights the previous week.

Blue Origin is also competing with SpaceX for the Artemis IV mission planned for 2028, which will land astronauts on the moon for the first time since 1972. The two companies are both developing lunar landers and have constructed large new facilities near Cape Canaveral to support crewed and cargo missions in partnership with NASA.

Flames continued burning at the launchpad for more than two hours after the explosion. Emergency officials reported no threat from fumes or other hazards. The cause of the explosion has not yet been determined, and the FAA has not indicated whether it will launch a new investigation into the incident.

cards.headline: Southwest Airlines reverses policy change for passengers requiring extra seats
cards.teaser: The airline updated its extra-seat policy for plus-size passengers four months after tightening the rules.
cards.body:
Southwest Airlines changed its policy regarding passengers who require additional seats. The update reverses a previous policy change that had been in place for four months and drew criticism.

The airline's earlier policy modification had applied to passengers who need more than one seat due to size. Southwest received backlash following implementation of the tightened seating requirements.

cards.headline: Oil prices post largest monthly decline since 2020
cards.teaser: Crude oil fell on hopes for a U.S.-Iran agreement, with Brent posting its biggest monthly loss in six years.
cards.body:
Oil prices recorded their steepest monthly decline since 2020, driven by investor optimism over potential U.S.-Iran peace negotiations. Brent crude fell 19% since the end of April, trading around $92 on Friday as markets reacted to reports of a breakthrough in talks aimed at extending a ceasefire.

The price drop reflected traders' assessment that a deal could ease geopolitical tensions in the region. Stock markets rallied alongside the oil decline as investors weighed the likelihood of an agreement between the two nations.

cards.headline: Fire at Penn Station injures five, disrupts rail service
cards.teaser: A maintenance train fire near Penn Station caused injuries and suspended service for multiple commuter rail lines.
cards.body:
A fire involving a maintenance train near Penn Station injured five people and caused major disruptions to rail service. The blaze occurred during rush hour, affecting Amtrak, NJ Transit, and Long Island Rail Road operations.

Service was suspended through Penn Station as crews responded to the fire. Amtrak later resumed operations through the station after the incident was brought under control.

cards.headline: China's clinical drug trials draw attention at international oncology meeting
cards.teaser: Chinese biotechnology advances highlighted at a Chicago gathering raised concerns about U.S. pharmaceutical dominance.
cards.body:
Clinical trials conducted in China are receiving increased attention at an international oncology conference in Chicago, highlighting the country's growing presence in biotechnology research and drug development.

The visibility of Chinese pharmaceutical work at the gathering reflects broader concerns in the United States about its declining dominance in the field. China's expanding biotechnology industry has intensified competition in global drug research and development.

cards.headline: SpaceX receives $6.45 billion in new Space Force contracts
cards.teaser: The contracts come as the company prepares for a public stock offering.
cards.body:
SpaceX has secured $6.45 billion in new contracts from the Space Force, the company announced as it prepares for its initial public offering. These agreements will deepen SpaceX's involvement in military space operations.

The contracts build on SpaceX's existing relationship with government agencies. According to the company's IPO filing, government work represented one-fifth of SpaceX's total revenue in 2025, underscoring the importance of defense and space sector work to the company's business.

cards.headline: Kenyan court blocks US plan to relocate Americans exposed to Ebola
cards.teaser: The ruling stops the Trump administration from transferring exposed individuals to Kenya.
cards.body:
A Kenyan court has blocked the Trump administration's plan to build a quarantine and treatment center in Kenya for Americans exposed to Ebola. The facility was intended to house Americans who may have been exposed to the virus during the outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

The White House had confirmed it was setting up the center in Kenya rather than bringing exposed Americans back to the United States for treatment and monitoring. However, some experts have criticized this approach, arguing that preventing Americans from returning home could hinder treatment efforts.

cards.headline: Indian court ruling on Google ad business draws support from founders
cards.teaser: Legal experts say the decision could force platforms to change how they handle trademarked keywords.
cards.body:
An Indian court has ruled on how Google handles trademarked keywords in its advertising system. The decision has drawn backing from founders who have previously criticized Google's ad practices.

Legal experts say the ruling could compel online platforms to reconsider their policies on trademarked terms. Founders have seized on the decision to renew their criticism of Google's advertising business model.

cards.headline: Nvidia and Microsoft tease new laptop processors ahead of tech conference
cards.teaser: Both companies, along with Arm, have posted messages about Nvidia's N1X chips.
cards.body:
Nvidia, Microsoft, and Arm are teasing Nvidia's new N1X laptop processors ahead of Computex this weekend. The Windows and Nvidia GeForce accounts posted "A new era of PC" on X, with Arm following suit with similar messaging.

Microsoft's Surface chief Pavan Davuluri also teased new hardware coming for developers, sharing a mysterious image of what appears to be a curved display edge. The coordinated posts signal major announcements related to Arm-powered laptop chips are imminent.

cards.headline: Researchers warn AI-assisted coding may not improve code quality
cards.teaser: Some programmers now refuse to work without artificial intelligence tools.
cards.body:
Programmers are increasingly relying on artificial intelligence to write code, with some refusing to work without these tools. While AI helps coders produce code faster, researchers have raised concerns about the quality of the output.

The researchers warn that AI-generated code may not be better than human-written code, despite the speed advantages. They caution this could create problems in the future for developers who become dependent on these tools without maintaining code quality standards.

cards.headline: Xbox will display PlayStation 5 availability at upcoming games showcase
cards.teaser: The company's chief content officer confirmed the cross-platform information will be shown.
cards.body:
Xbox Chief Content Officer Matt Booty announced that the upcoming Xbox Games Showcase will display PlayStation 5 availability information for games being presented at the event. This move highlights which titles will release on competing platforms alongside Xbox.

Booty also confirmed that Project Helix will not be discussed during the June showcase. The event is expected to feature presentations on games including Gears of War E-Day and Fable.

hero.headline: Teenager Fonseca defeats Djokovic at French Open, ending Grand Slam bid
hero.body:
Novak Djokovic's bid for a 25th Grand Slam title ended at the French Open when 19-year-old Brazilian Joao Fonseca defeated him in a remarkable five-set comeback on Court Philippe-Chatrier. The victory ensures this year's tournament will crown a first-time men's Grand Slam champion.

Fonseca won 4-6, 4-6, 6-3, 7-5, 7-5 after four hours and 53 minutes of intense competition. Djokovic had controlled the early stages, winning the first two sets and building what appeared to be a commanding position. However, the 39-year-old's physical condition deteriorated as the match progressed. After four hours on court, Djokovic vomited into the red clay during the later stages, struggling against an opponent two decades younger.

The Brazilian teenager's refusal to surrender transformed the match. Despite trailing by two sets, Fonseca mounted an extraordinary comeback that only the second player in tennis history has achieved against Djokovic. Statistically, Djokovic's record in best-of-five matches after winning the first two sets stood at 301-1 before this loss.

"I didn't, really," Fonseca said when asked if he believed he could win from two sets down. "It's my first time stepping on court with him, he's a legend. I'm just really happy." He added that he was simply focused on hitting the ball hard and was not thinking about the magnitude of the occasion. Fonseca also credited the changing light as the match extended into evening, noting that the court slowed down, which helped his game. He highlighted his serving performance, saying he was surprised by his ability to hit aces.

Fonseca acknowledged his mother's birthday and thanked Brazilian fans for their support throughout the match. The teenager had only played two five-set matches in his professional career before this encounter, yet he showed no signs of fatigue or cramping during the final sets against the legendary Serbian player.

This result continues a pattern of upsets at Roland Garros, where several higher-seeded players have fallen to younger competitors. The defeat highlights the growing competitiveness among emerging players on the professional tennis circuit and signals Fonseca's emergence among tennis's elite.

For Djokovic, the loss represents another setback in his pursuit of extending his Grand Slam record. At 39, managing the physical demands of five-set matches against top competitors appears increasingly challenging. His exit from the tournament opens the remaining competition to a new generation of players competing for their first major championship.

With Djokovic eliminated, Fonseca advances to face either Casper Ruud or Tommy Paul in the next round.

cards.headline: Thunder's Jalen Williams ruled out for Game 7 against Spurs
cards.teaser: Oklahoma City will be without guard Jalen Williams for the decisive Western Conference Finals game due to a hamstring injury.
cards.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder will play Game 7 of the Western Conference Finals without Jalen Williams, who has been ruled out due to a hamstring injury.

The Thunder face elimination after losing Game 6 to the San Antonio Spurs 118-91 on Thursday. Victor Wembanyama led the Spurs with 28 points and 10 rebounds in the victory. Game 7 is scheduled for Saturday in Oklahoma City, with the winner advancing to the NBA Finals to face the New York Knicks.

cards.headline: Arsenal faces Paris Saint-Germain in Champions League final
cards.teaser: Arsenal will take on PSG in the Champions League final, with tactical preparation under scrutiny ahead of the match.
cards.body:
Arsenal prepares to meet Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League final on Saturday. Mikel Arteta has confirmed that Dutch defender Jurrien Timber is fit to start the match after recovering from a groin injury that sidelined him for over two months.

Arsenal players including Leandro Trossard, Declan Rice, and Eberechi Eze have reflected on what winning the trophy would mean to them. BBC Sport's tactics correspondent has examined how Arsenal's approach could be decisive against Paris Saint-Germain in the final.

cards.headline: Jose Mourinho returns to Real Madrid as manager
cards.teaser: Real Madrid has hired Jose Mourinho for a second stint as head coach, raising questions about his relationship with star forward Vinicius Junior.
cards.body:
Jose Mourinho has agreed to return to Real Madrid as manager for his second spell with the club. The Portuguese coach previously led the Spanish giants and now returns to the role.

How Mourinho manages his relationship with Brazil forward Vinicius Junior will be one of the most closely watched aspects of his tenure. The experienced manager's handling of the talented attacker is expected to be a key focus during his time in charge.

cards.headline: Canada names World Cup squad with Alphonso Davies
cards.teaser: Head coach Jesse Marsch selected Bayern Munich defender Alphonso Davies for what he called the best Canada squad ever assembled for the World Cup.
cards.body:
Canada head coach Jesse Marsch has named his World Cup squad, including Bayern Munich defender Alphonso Davies. Marsch called it the best Canada squad ever assembled for the tournament.

Davies will be among the key players representing Canada at this summer's World Cup.

cards.headline: Pentagon offers World Cup fight tickets to troops meeting fitness standards
cards.teaser: Military personnel must meet weight standards to receive free tickets to a UFC event at the White House, according to Department of Defense memos.
cards.body:
The Pentagon is recruiting service members to attend UFC fights at the White House, with eligibility tied to meeting fitness criteria. Internal memos show troops must satisfy weight standards to qualify for free tickets to the event.

The White House will host the UFC fight, with specific attendance requirements outlined for military personnel. Troops who do not meet the fitness standards will not be eligible for the complimentary tickets. The event is scheduled as part of activities at the executive residence.

cards.headline: White Sox walk off Tigers in 10 innings on Vargas homer
cards.teaser: Miguel Vargas hit his first career walk-off home run in the 10th inning to give Chicago a 4-3 victory over Detroit.
cards.body:
The Chicago White Sox defeated the Detroit Tigers 4-3 in 10 innings after Miguel Vargas delivered his first career walk-off home run. The dramatic finish came before a packed crowd at the ballpark.

Vargas's homer ended the game after the White Sox lost slugger Munetaka Murakami to a hamstring injury earlier in the contest. The victory salvaged what had been a difficult evening

hero.headline: Star Wars Editor Marcia Lucas Dies at 80
hero.body:
Marcia Lucas, the Oscar-winning film editor who worked on the original Star Wars, died Wednesday at her home in Rancho Mirage, California. She was 80. Lucas had been battling metastatic cancer.

Lucasfilm released a statement expressing sorrow at her death. Lucas was one of three editors who shared the Academy Award for editing the 1977 film Star Wars. She was formerly married to Star Wars creator George Lucas.

Beyond Star Wars, Lucas edited several notable films of the 1970s. Her work included Martin Scorsese's Taxi Driver, which was released in 1976. She also edited American Graffiti, the 1973 film directed by George Lucas that became a cultural touchstone and launched multiple careers in Hollywood.

Lucas's editing on Star Wars played a significant role in shaping the final film. The original footage was transformed through the editing process, with Lucas among those who helped create the pacing and structure that made the film a phenomenon. Her contributions to the original Star Wars trilogy extended beyond the first film, though her work on the 1977 movie remains her most recognized achievement.

The film editor's career spanned a transformative period in American cinema. She worked during an era when editors wielded substantial creative influence over final cuts. Her collaborations with both George Lucas and Scorsese placed her at the center of some of the most important films of the decade.

Lucas retired from film editing in the early 1980s. She maintained a low public profile in the decades that followed, rarely giving interviews about her work or her time in the film industry. Her death removes one of the last surviving key creative figures from the original Star Wars production.

The Academy Award she received for Star Wars recognized her technical skill and creative vision. That Oscar win cemented her place in film history, even as she chose to step away from the industry that had brought her recognition.

cards.headline: Music Executive Clive Davis Hospitalized in New York
cards.teaser: The 94-year-old record industry veteran was admitted to a New York City hospital following a respiratory issue.
cards.body:
Clive Davis, the music executive who shaped multiple generations of popular music, was hospitalized in New York City on Friday evening. The 94-year-old was admitted following a respiratory issue.

Davis built his career discovering and developing major artists across multiple decades. His influence extended across various genres, and he remained active in the music industry into his nineties.

cards.headline: Frankie Valli Cancels Remaining 2026 Concert Dates
cards.teaser: The 92-year-old singer announced he is canceling the rest of his tour this year due to health issues.
cards.body:
Frankie Valli announced Friday that he is canceling all remaining concert dates for 2026 to focus on his health. The 92-year-old singer, known for his decades with The Four Seasons, shared the news on social media and apologized to fans who purchased tickets.

Despite his age, Valli has remained devoted to touring throughout his career and continued performing into his nineties before making this decision.

cards.headline: Paul McCartney Reflects on Family During Beatles Fame
cards.teaser: The musician discussed how his family helped ground him during the height of Beatlemania.
cards.body:
At 83, Paul McCartney is reflecting on his past for his new solo album, The Boys of Dungeon Lane. The project draws inspiration from formative memories, family singalongs, and moments from his own life story.

McCartney discussed how looking back has given him hope during turbulent times that mirror today's world. His nostalgic album was inspired by old bandmates and represents his continued gift for melody and storytelling.

cards.headline: Bill Maher Criticizes Trump Freedom 250 Concert Series
cards.teaser: The comedian devoted part of his Friday show to mocking the National Mall concert series planned for America's 250th birthday.
cards.body:
Bill Maher used his Friday night show to criticize President Trump's Freedom 250 concert series, scheduled for the National Mall in Washington to commemorate America's 250th birthday on July 4th. The event has been plagued by performer withdrawals, with at least seven of the nine featured musical acts dropping out within 48 hours of the lineup announcement.

Among those who backed out were Martina McBride, Morris Day, Young MC, and Bret Michaels. Michaels cited a deteriorating atmosphere around the event and threats being made as reasons for his withdrawal. Maher's monologue focused on the concert series before he interviewed Neil deGrasse Tyson later in the program.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Councilwoman Pushes for Expanded Film Tax Credits
cards.teaser: Nithya Raman urged gubernatorial candidates to support uncapped tax incentives for film and television production in California.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Councilwoman Nithya Raman called on candidates for governor to support uncapped tax incentives for film and television production. She made the appeal Friday outside Radford Studios with several entertainment industry figures.

Raman appeared alongside television creators Mike Schur, Cord Jefferson, and Kay Cannon, who support her mayoral campaign. She said California must ensure Hollywood remains competitive as other states and countries offer production incentives.

cards.headline: DJ John Summit Announces Fall Arena Tour
cards.teaser: The electronic music producer is bringing his CTRL ESCAPE tour to arenas across the United States and Canada this fall.
cards.body:
John Summit announced plans for an arena tour across the United States and Canada this fall. The DJ will bring his CTRL ESCAPE tour to multiple cities.

Tickets for the tour are now available for purchase. Summit has built a following in electronic music and is expanding to larger venues with the arena tour.

hero.headline: White House releases memo saying Trump in excellent health after annual physical
hero.body:
President Trump remains in excellent health, according to a memo from his physician released by the White House on Friday following his annual physical examination earlier in the week.

Trump visited Walter Reed National Military Medical Center on Tuesday for the routine checkup. During his time there, he underwent cardiac, neurological, dermatologic and other types of examinations. The White House confirmed these tests were completed as part of the standard annual physical for a sitting president.

The physician's memo stated that Trump remains fit to serve. The White House released the assessment late Friday evening. However, the memo did not provide detailed results from individual tests or examinations. Instead, it offered only a summary of the president's overall health status, covering multiple areas of physical health including cardiovascular and neurological function.

The annual physical examination is standard procedure for sitting presidents. Walter Reed National Military Medical Center in Bethesda, Maryland, typically conducts these evaluations.

Independent physicians not affiliated with the White House have raised questions about certain physical observations. These medical observers have pointed to recurrent bruises on Trump's hands and swelling in his legs that have been visible during recent public appearances. These independent assessments suggest these physical signs warrant explanation from medical professionals.

The official memo from Trump's physician did not address these specific concerns raised by independent medical observers. The White House has not responded to questions about the bruises and leg swelling that outside physicians have noted.

The White House medical reports focused on Trump's fitness to carry out his duties rather than providing comprehensive information about all observable physical characteristics. The memo's release represents the White House's official statement on the president's current health status following the comprehensive examination at Walter Reed.

The timing of the memo's release late Friday evening is consistent with how the White House often distributes routine administrative announcements. The physical examination itself had been conducted earlier in the week, allowing time for the physician to compile the assessment and for White House officials to prepare the memo for public release.

The lack of detailed test results in the released memo is not unusual, as presidential health information typically remains largely private. The White House customarily releases only summary assessments rather than comprehensive medical data. However, the gap between the physician's overall assessment and the concerns raised by independent observers has drawn attention to what specific findings might not be included in the public memo.

cards.headline: Federal judge reopens Trump's $10 billion IRS lawsuit for further review
cards.teaser: A federal judge agreed to reopen President Trump's suit against the IRS after intervenors challenged a settlement agreement.
cards.body:
A federal judge in Florida agreed to reopen President Trump's $10 billion lawsuit against the IRS. The judge sided with intervenors who challenged a settlement agreement that would have dismissed the case in exchange for creating an "anti-weaponization" fund.

The decision allows the case to proceed for further scrutiny. A separate federal judge in Virginia has already temporarily blocked the Trump administration from transferring money into the $1.8 billion fund while legal challenges continue.

cards.headline: Trump endorses Pam Evette for South Carolina governor over Rep. Nancy Mace
cards.teaser: President Trump backed Lt. Gov. Pam Evette in the South Carolina governor's race, snubbing Rep. Nancy Mace's campaign.
cards.body:
President Trump endorsed Lt. Gov. Pam Evette in the South Carolina gubernatorial race on Friday, choosing not to support Rep. Nancy Mace, who is also running for the Republican nomination. Trump announced his backing on Truth Social.

In his endorsement statement, Trump praised Evette as an "America First Patriot" and described her as a good friend, fighter, and winner.

cards.headline: U.S. military kills three in strike on suspected drug vessel in eastern Pacific
cards.teaser: U.S. Southern Command said it struck a boat accused of carrying drugs in the eastern Pacific Ocean.
cards.body:
The U.S. military carried out another strike Friday on a boat in the eastern Pacific Ocean, killing three men. U.S. Southern Command said the vessel was engaged in narco-trafficking operations and operated by a designated terrorist organization.

This marks the third attack this week as part of an ongoing campaign against suspected drug boats in the Caribbean Sea and eastern Pacific. The strikes have resulted in a death toll exceeding 200 people over several months.

cards.headline: Top U.S. military commander meets with Cuban military officials
cards.teaser: The head of U.S. Southern Command met with senior Cuban military leaders near Guantanamo Bay.
cards.body:
Original Card Text (Unchanged)

The head of U.S. Southern Command met with senior leaders of the Cuban military amid heightened tensions between the two governments. Commander Gen. Francis L. Donovan joined Cuba's First Deputy Minister of the Chief of the General Staff Roberto Legra Sotolongo and other leaders near Naval Station Guantanamo Bay.

Southcom announced the meeting took place as President Trump has increased pressure on the island. The meeting brought together military officials from both countries at a time of strained diplomatic relations.

---

Note: The additional source material provided covers unrelated topics (Asia defense summit, Israel-Lebanon meetings, and voting order). Since no new confirmed facts about the Cuba-U.S. military meeting are present in the source material, the original card text is returned unchanged.

cards.headline: Talarico leads Paxton by 3 points in Texas Senate race poll
cards.teaser: A new poll shows the Democratic candidate holds a slight edge over the Republican in the Texas Senate race.
cards.body:
State Rep. James Talarico holds a slight lead over Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton in a new poll released after the runoff. The poll from Texas Public Opinion Research showed 47 percent of likely general election voters backed Talarico compared with 44 percent for Paxton.

The Democratic candidate's three-point advantage falls within typical polling margins. The survey measured support among likely voters in the general election contest.

cards.headline: Treasury Secretary Bessent says Trump should appear on proposed $250 bill
cards.teaser: Scott Bessent endorsed a proposal to feature President Trump on a $250 bill commemorating the U.S. semiquincentennial.
cards.body:
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is pushing Congress to approve a $250 bill featuring President Trump's portrait to celebrate the nation's 250th anniversary of independence. The proposal would require changing federal law that currently prohibits living people from appearing on U.S. currency.

Speaking at a White House news conference, Bessent said the Treasury Department has already begun preparing for the possibility of issuing the new currency. Democrats have vowed to block the measure.
